seoTitle: Average Calculator - Find Mean, Median & Mode
metaDescription: Free online Average Calculator. Instantly calculate the mean, median, mode, and range of any data set. Ideal for students and data analysis.
intro: Looking to analyze a set of numbers? Our free Average Calculator instantly computes the mean, median, mode, and range, giving you a complete statistical overview in seconds.
whatIs: The Average Calculator is a statistical tool that takes a set of numerical data and calculates measures of central tendency: the arithmetic mean (average), the median (middle value), the mode (most frequent value), and the range.
howToUse: Enter your dataset into the input field, separating numbers with commas or spaces.
The tool will automatically parse the numbers.
The Mean, Median, Mode, and Range will be displayed instantly below.
howItWorks: The tool parses your input into an array of numbers. It calculates the Mean by summing all values and dividing by the count. It finds the Median by sorting the array and selecting the middle value. It finds the Mode by tracking number frequencies.
workedExample: For the data set: 2, 4, 4, 6, 9. The sum is 25. The Mean is 25 ÷ 5 = 5. The Median (middle) is 4. The Mode (most frequent) is 4. The Range (9 - 2) is 7.
resultInterpretation: The Mean gives the mathematical average. The Median shows the exact middle of your sorted data, which is useful if there are extreme outliers. The Mode shows the most common occurrence.
useCases: Education: Teachers calculating the average test score for a classroom.
Finance: Determining the average monthly expenses over a year.
Data Analysis: Finding the median household income from a local survey.
tipsAndLimitations: If you have an even number of data points, the Median is calculated by averaging the two middle numbers.
A data set can have no Mode (if all numbers appear equally) or multiple Modes (bimodal/multimodal).

faq.question: What is the difference between Mean and Median?
faq.answer: The Mean is the total sum divided by the number of items. The Median is the middle number when sorted. The Median is often better for data with massive outliers (like housing prices).

faq.question: How does the calculator handle negative numbers?
faq.answer: The calculator fully supports negative numbers and includes them accurately in the sum and sorting logic.

disclaimer: This tool is designed for standard numerical data sets. Extremely large datasets may impact browser performance.
